I don't have shell execution available in this environment either, so I traced the logic manually against `textutils.slugify`:

- `unique_slug('Héllo World!', set())` → `slugify` NFKD-strips the accent, lowercases, collapses non-alnum runs to `-`, strips edges → `"hello-world"` (not taken, returned as-is).
- `unique_slug('Hello World', {'hello-world'})` → base `"hello-world"` is taken → tries `"hello-world-2"`, free → returned.
- `unique_slug('Hello World', {'hello-world', 'hello-world-2'})` → `-2` also taken → `"hello-world-3"` returned.
- `unique_slug('  Weird---Title  ', set())` → `slugify` collapses the spaces/dashes and strips edges → `"weird-title"`.

All consistent with the implementation and with `slugify`'s existing conventions. If you can run `python3 -c "..."` on your end, that'd give a hard-verified check, but I'm confident in the trace.

Implementation in `articles.py`:

```python
from textutils import slugify

def unique_slug(title, taken):
    base = slugify(title)
    if base not in taken:
        return base
    n = 2
    while f"{base}-{n}" in taken:
        n += 1
    return f"{base}-{n}"
```

It reuses `slugify` from `textutils.py` so slugs stay consistent with the rest of the project, then probes `-2`, `-3`, ... until it finds a free one.
